correctness.rationale: At a complete reset cycle of length L, conditional Brownian area is centered Gaussian with variance 2DL^3/3. The exact Laplace transform E exp[-(D/3)k²L³] has small-k exponent Γ(1-α/3)(D/3)^(α/3)|k|^(2α/3) for 2<α<3; the renewal strong law N_T/T→(α-1)/α turns complete-cycle partial-sum limits into the stated physical-time stable constant. At α=3 the borderline transform 1-φ(k)~(D/3)k² log(1/[(D/3)k²]) yields variance 4D/9 in the sqrt(T log T) weak Gaussian limit. For α>3, E L³=α/(α-3) produces the finite-variance CLT. Stationary equilibrium-age/residual integration gives Cov(X_0,X_h)=D/μ E[(L-h)_+²], evaluating to the asserted h≤1 polynomial and h≥1 power tail. Integrating 2∫_0^T(T-h)Cov dh independently yields 4D/3 at α=3, hence a real factor-three nonuniform-integrability anomaly. Initial and terminal partial excursions have tight stationary area laws and vanish after diverging scaling. Independent direct renewal quadrature tested 15 cases; it is not an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The signed time-averaged displacement is a canonical transport observable, and the exact stable-to-critical Gaussian boundary at α=3 together with the factor-three failure of second-moment convergence distinguishes typical fluctuations from rare long reset gaps. The stationary covariance power law supplies a separate physical-memory interpretation. This is more than a routine application of finite-variance CLT; it identifies a nonuniform-integrability boundary with explicit constants.

final_claim: For stationary exactly-reset Brownian motion with Pareto cycle-tail index α>2, the signed time-integral has a symmetric 2α/3-stable weak limit for 2<α<3, a Gaussian sqrt(T log T) limit of variance 4D/9 at α=3 despite normalized variance 4D/3, and the ordinary Gaussian limit for α>3; stationary autocovariance is explicit.
limitations: The Gaussian weak limit at α=3 does not have converging normalized second moments.
No result for α≤2, nonstationary initialization, unsigned excursion areas or dependence across cycles.
